title: Hospitality
sourceBasis: World English Bible — 66-book Old and New Testament Scripture text already installed in Iron Sharpener
definition: Hospitality is the generous welcome of others through love, service, presence, and practical care. God’s people are called to open their lives to others, not merely those who can repay or benefit them.
summary: Hospitality is the generous welcome of others through love, service, presence, and practical care. God’s people are called to open their lives to others, not merely those who can repay or benefit them.
christFocus: Jesus Christ welcomes sinners, strangers, the needy, and the rejected into the grace of God. Christian hospitality reflects His open-handed mercy and the welcome believers have received through Him.

studySections.heading: Doctrine in Summary
studySections.content:
Hospitality is a biblical expression of love. It is not merely entertaining or impressing guests, but welcoming others with practical care and generosity.

Scripture calls believers to practice hospitality without grumbling. The heart matters. Hospitality should reflect glad service, not pride, resentment, or performance.

Jesus taught His people to welcome those who cannot repay them. This corrects self-serving hospitality that only opens the door to the impressive, comfortable, or useful.

The early church practiced shared life, meals, generosity, and welcome. Hospitality became one way the Gospel was made visible in ordinary homes and relationships.

studySections.heading: Why This Matters
studySections.content:
Many people are lonely, overlooked, or disconnected. Hospitality can become a powerful witness that says, in practice, that people matter before God.

This doctrine also challenges comfort and isolation. Christian love often requires opening time, space, attention, and resources for the good of others.

studySections.heading: Discipleship and Application
studySections.content: Practice hospitality in ways that fit your season and ability. Welcome others with humility, not performance. Share meals, space, time, prayer, conversation, and practical help, especially with those who are lonely, new, weak, or unable to repay you.
